title: Model Fit & Token Economics Playbook
summary: Practical playbook used in a customer-facing workshop to decide model family, quantization approach, and prompt/pipeline architecture with explicit token-cost tradeoffs and rollout steps for a mid-market SaaS POC.
body:
Objective:
- Produce a short, reproducible decision path for picking a model variant and quantization profile that meets a target latency (p95 < 400ms), accuracy (task-specific F1 or ROUGE targets), and per-request token cost budget for a chat+extract POC.

Customer context (notes from pre-workshop):
- Mid-market CRM vendor with multi-turn chat, entity extraction, and short-form summarization.
- SLA: interactive latency for 95th percentile <= 400ms in dedicated deployment; cost target ~ $0.002 per 1k tokens at scale (aspirational).
- Data sensitivity: logs must not leave VPC for private deployment later — impacts model caching strategy and on-prem quant choices.

Constraints and non-negotiables:
- No external model-hosting allowed for sensitive flows (must support Redwood Private).
- On initial POC, we can use hosted for prototyping but must reproduce behavior in Private with same model family + quant profile.
- Customer expects canary rollout and simple fallback to smaller model on overload.

Model selection matrix (first-order sweep):
- Candidate families: Llama 2 family (7B/13B), Mistral medium, MPT-30B, openbaize distill variants.
- Heuristic mapping: retrieval/extraction-heavy -> prefer 7B-13B with tuned prompts + reranker; long-context summarization -> 13B+ or MPT-30B if latency budget allows.
- Tradeoffs captured: model_size | baseline_perplexity | kv-memory | expected_latency_8bit | compression_risk
  - 7B: low cost, excellent latency after 4-bit/8-bit quant, slightly worse on long-range coherence
  - 13B: sweet spot for multi-turn accuracy, moderate cost
  - 30B+: high quality but hard to hit 400ms p95 without aggressive batching or larger infra

Recommended proto plan (week 0–2):
1) Baseline: run 7B float32 (hosted) to gather token distributions, average prompt + history length.
2) Cost projection: instrument token counts per request; estimate monthly tokens at expected query volume.
3) Run small sweep: 7B-8bit, 7B-4bit, 13B-8bit. Measure p50/p95 latency, token throughput, and answer-quality on curated eval set (20 representative sessions).
4) If 13B-8bit meets latency and quality targets, prefer it. Else pick 7B-4bit with quality-boost via prompt-engineered scaffolding and a micro-reranker.

Quantization strategy (practical notes):
- Start with 8-bit (Q8) for the first reproducible jump: predictable, minimal quality regression for autoregressive LM use.
- Only move to 4-bit (QLoRA/FP4/FP4*, depending on runtime) when cost delta is material and we have a small finetune/LoRA budget to recover degradation.
- For on-prem Private deployments, prefer integer-backed 8-bit kernels (faster on A100/4090 stacks) unless vendor runtime supports efficient 4-bit. Document exact kernel names used.
- KV cache considerations: quantized models sometimes blow up KV cache memory if conversion changes dtype; validate on long-history sequences (16–32 turns).

Prompt & pipeline tuning checklist:
- Token budget: compute expected tokens = average prompt_tokens + avg_response_tokens + prefix_tokens (system messages + safety layers). Aim for < 300 tokens for interactive flows when using 7B variants.
- Prompt scaffolding: move heavy instructions into a short system message + use few-shot examples only in reranker stage. Keep per-turn prompts minimal (1–3 sentences).
- Multi-stage pipeline recommended:
  1) Fast intent classifier (tiny distilled classifier, returning routing flags).
  2) Main generator (7B/13B quantized) for conversational output.
  3) Lightweight extractor (regex + small LM) or reranker for high-precision entity extraction.
  4) Final filter + deterministic post-processing.
- Reranking: prefer n-best generation with a small 2–4 candidate reranker (tiny LM or scoring head). Rerankers are cheaper if run at embedding or smaller-scale and reduce required main model quality ceiling.

Batching and caching heuristics for POC: 
- Use short-time adaptive batching (20–50ms latency window) on Dedicated to increase GPU utilization without affecting p95 too much.
- Prefix caching: if many requests share identical system prompt + few-shot, cache KV states. For multi-tenant POC, ensure cache keys include tenant + model-version.

Metrics to capture during sweep:
- Latency: p50, p90, p95 token-generation and end-to-end.
- Token economics: tokens_in, tokens_out, tokens_total, cost-per-request (projected from cost-per-token estimates).
- Quality: task-specific metric (F1 for extraction, ROUGE-L for summarization), human rating (5-point) for N=20 sample sessions.
- Resource: GPU mem, VRAM footprint after quant, CPU overhead for pre/post processing.

Quick cost calculation example (for decision-making):
- Baseline numbers collected: avg tokens/request = 180; avg responses = 120 tokens.
- If hosted cost estimate = $0.0008 per 1k tokens for 7B-8bit equivalence -> per-request token cost = (180+120)/1000 * $0.0008 = $0.00024.
- Multiply by expected QPS and monthly volume to decide Reserved vs Hosted for Dedicated.

Rollout & fallback policy (POC -> Prod):
- Canary: route 5% traffic to quantized model variant + compare quality signals and error rates for 72h.
- Fallback: if p95 > SLA or quality delta > threshold, automatically downshift to smaller model (7B-8bit -> fallback micro-model) and flag for human review.
- Audit: record request hashes and model-version; for private deployments ensure logs are stored in customer-controlled S3/GCS.

Experiment log (short entries):
- 2024-10-08: Baseline hosted run with 7B-f32; avg lat p95 = 820ms (too high), tokens/request = 210.
- 2024-10-15: 7B-Q8 on A10G equivalent -> p95 = 310ms; quality delta negligible on extraction tasks.
- 2024-10-22: 13B-Q8 on same infra -> p95 = 640ms; better summarization scores but fails latency target.
- Decision: proceed with 7B-Q8 as primary + micro-reranker for extraction improvements.

Open questions & risks:
- Will 7B-Q8 generalize to the long-tail of user prompts for summarization? (needs 200-session smoke test)
- On Private/Azure on-prem infra, do we have equivalent optimized kernels for Q8/Q4? Need SRE/infra validation.
- Security: how do we rotate/model keys when running LoRA weights locally in Private?

Next steps (actionable):
- Priya: assemble 20-session eval set by 2024-10-11 (ticket JIRA-SE-3421).
- Diego: spin 7B-Q8 benchmark on customer-sim infra, measure p95 & KV footprint by 2024-10-14.
- Ava: prepare canary routing policy draft and rollback thresholds; share with SRE by 2024-10-18.

Appendix: useful commands & artifacts
- Local benchmark script: github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks#se-infra-run
- Small eval template (CSV columns): session_id, prompt, expected_entities, expected_summary, human_score
- Quick reference: when to pick 4-bit: only if cost reduction > 30% and we can LoRA-recover quality with <= 2k steps.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep prompts modular, prefer post-processing extractors to heavy few-shot context.
- Document exact kernel versions used on infra; small changes yield big latency differences on quantized models.
- Emphasize reproducibility: commit random seeds for generation tests.

End of playbook.
